svg.text: Write the click to the stream first, then record the impression id in the cache, so a cache failure can't lose a click

svg.text: Aggregates are upserted with SUM, so partial writes from sub-partitions combine correctly

svg.text: Data is already aggregated, so queries are fast

svg.text: Large windows hit the pre-aggregated tables; drill down to minutes only when needed

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • Scale: 10M active ads, peak 10k clicks/s (average ≈ 1k/s ≈ 100M clicks/day); a 5-minute batch is only ~3M events / 300 MB, so Spark isn't needed for volume

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • Why not one DB for events and queries: GROUP BY over raw rows won't give sub-second answers. Why OLAP, not time-series DB: millions of ad ids and multi-dimensional slices

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • Hot shards: for a viral ad, key = AdId:0..N so one shard isn't overwhelmed; Flink strips the suffix before writing
